name: Photoreal cinematic (Blender plates)
description: Path-traced plates from the Blender engine with real lenses and depth of field, moved by depth-parallax camera moves. Dark neutral grade, glass cards, one warm accent. No people (see docs/PHOTOREAL.md).
rules: The picture is a path-traced plate: HDRI light, PBR materials, a real lens (35-50 mm look, f/1.8-2.8) with depth of field. Never flat-lit.
One warm accent, used on the single most important word; the rest is neutral.
Camera moves are slow and motivated (push 4-12 percent, orbit under 8 degrees, crane under 10 percent); a hold of 2.5 s is fine. No whip pans on parallax plates.
Cards are glass panels placed beside or below the subject, never over it. Overlays dock to the card edge.
Grade: AgX, lifted blacks, bloom only on highlights, fine grain. Keep skin tones out: this engine has no people.
camera_language: Slow push-ins on the subject, one orbit reveal per scene, rack focus between foreground and subject via the focus point, handheld 0.2-0.4 for documentary feel.
typography: Serif italic for places, mono for dates.
audio_direction: calm bed, paper slide whooshes, stamp on dates
pitfalls: Parallax over 8 degrees tears edges at depth jumps: use a Blender sequence for bigger moves.
A flat HDRI with no key light looks like a catalogue; add one warm area light for direction.
Over-bloom turns glass into fog; keep bloom under 0.35.
